label: Illustrative, authored from public trial information
short_title: Pozelimab + cemdisiran, cemdisiran alone, or placebo by subcutaneous injection, geographic atrophy secondary to AMD (SIENNA)
practice_basis: standard follow-up of geographic atrophy not treated with intravitreal therapy
why_chosen: A recruiting Regeneron-led Phase 3 outside oncology with the most registered U.S. sites of Regeneron's non-oncology Phase 3s (158 at fetch). Its registry entry names concrete, codable procedures (fundus autofluorescence, visual acuity, a screening throat culture for meningococcal carriage, HbA1c, required meningococcal and pneumococcal vaccination) and fixed endpoint weeks (52 and 104).
dosing: All study drugs by subcutaneous injection (registry); the interval is not in the registry, every 4 weeks is an assumption
registry_notes: Registry adverse-event time frames run to weeks 140 and 296 (a later period); only the double-masked period to week 104 is scheduled here.
standard_care_reference: Eye exam with OCT and fundus autofluorescence about every 6 months for geographic atrophy that is not treated with intravitreal therapy (the registry excludes recent intravitreal treatment)
Visual acuity is part of the eye exam; no protocol refraction, low-contrast acuity or contrast-sensitivity testing
Fluorescein angiography only when new neovascularization is suspected, not routinely
No routine blood tests, throat cultures or vaccinations because of geographic atrophy
No systemic drug administration for geographic atrophy
standard_care_source: Authored reference for monitoring untreated geographic atrophy; the 6-month interval is an authoring assumption, not a published guideline value. Used only to apply rules R3 and R4. Not a coverage determination.

assumptions: The registry does not publish a schedule of assessments. Visit weeks, windows, the dosing interval and the lab panel are authored, not copied from the protocol.
Dosing every 4 weeks from Day 1 to week 100 (26 dosing visits). The registry gives the route (subcutaneous) but not the interval.

Double-dummy masking: every participant receives two blinded injections per dosing visit (pozelimab-or-placebo and cemdisiran-or-placebo), so all three arms look alike. The registry says only that masking is quadruple.
Study drugs are supplied by the sponsor and never billed; only their administration (96372) appears.

Imaging (fundus autofluorescence and OCT) and a comprehensive eye exam at screening and weeks 24, 52, 76 and 104, about every 6 months. The registry names FAF to weeks 52 and 104 but not the imaging visits in between.

An intermediate eye exam (92012) at every other dosing visit as an ocular safety check. These are research (R4): the standard-care reference gives one exam about every 6 months, which the comprehensive exams at screening and weeks 24, 52, 76 and 104 already count.
Images are sent to a central reading center for lesion measurement (common in geographic atrophy trials; the registry does not name one).
Safety labs (blood count, chemistry) at screening and weeks 12, 24, 52, 76 and 104. Not in the registry.

Vaccinations: one MenACWY dose, one MenB dose and one pneumococcal dose at screening. The registry requires 'the full series'; later doses are not modelled. Vaccine products have no CMS PFS or CLFS amount in the loaded rate card and are shown unpriced; only the administration (90471, 90472) is priced.
Pneumococcal vaccination is labelled research (R2) because the protocol requires it; a reviewer may relabel it routine for participants for whom it is routinely recommended.
Visual-function tests (ETDRS BCVA, LC-qVA, LL-LC-qVA, qCSF) have no CPT code and no published Medicare amount; they are listed unpriced as research items to be negotiated, not given a number.
The period after week 104 (adverse events to weeks 140 and 296) is not scheduled, and there is no separate early-termination visit.

at.reason: A comprehensive eye exam is standard care for a patient with geographic atrophy (the standard-care reference gives one about every 6 months).
Exams about every 6 months match the standard-care reference for untreated geographic atrophy.

The protocol examines the eye at every 4-weekly dosing visit; the standard-care reference gives about one exam every 6 months, already counted at screening and weeks 24, 52, 76 and 104. These extra exams are research.
ETDRS BCVA, low-contrast and low-luminance acuity and contrast sensitivity are registry endpoints at baseline, week 52 and week 104; standard care does not test them.
Fundus autofluorescence about every 6 months matches the standard-care reference for monitoring geographic atrophy.
OCT about every 6 months matches the standard-care reference (it also checks for new neovascularization).
Angiography to exclude neovascularization for eligibility (registry exclusion 2); standard care does not do it routinely.
Sending images to a central reading center exists only for the trial's lesion-growth endpoint.
HbA1c to check eligibility (registry exclusion 13); not part of geographic atrophy care.
Safety labs exist because of the investigational complement inhibitor; untreated geographic atrophy needs no blood tests.
